u5-l1.0.en.en: What do we need for the party?

u5-l1.0.note.en: Emma and Lucia are planning a party (oslava). potrebovať = to need: potrebuj**em**, potrebuj**eš**, potrebuj**e**…
u5-l1.0.note.t: Emma va Lusiya bazm (oslava) rejalashtiryapti. potrebovať = kerak boʻlmoq: potrebuj**em**, potrebuj**eš**, potrebuj**e**…

u5-l1.6.note.en: minerálka is short for minerálna voda.
u5-l1.6.note.t: minerálka — minerálna voda (mineral suv) soʻzining qisqa shakli.

u5-l1.9.note.en: You know **stáť** from unit 4: Šunka stojí tri eurá. = The ham costs three euros.
u5-l1.9.note.t: **stáť** sizga 4-boʻlimdan tanish: Šunka stojí tri eurá. = Vetchina uch yevro turadi.

u5-l1.10.why.en: Káva is one thing, so stáť takes the one-thing form: **stojí**. Stoja is for two or more things, stojím for ja.
u5-l1.10.why.t: Káva — bitta narsa, shuning uchun stáť bitta narsa shaklida keladi: **stojí**. Stoja ikki va undan ortiq narsa uchun, stojím esa ja uchun.

u5-l1.13.note.en: kúpiť = to buy: kúpim, kúpiš, kúpi… It usually points to the future: “I'll buy”. čerstvý = fresh.
u5-l1.13.note.t: kúpiť = sotib olmoq: kúpim, kúpiš, kúpi… Bu shakl odatda kelajakni bildiradi: «sotib olaman». čerstvý = yangi (ovqat haqida: yangi non; nový esa yangi narsa: yangi telefon).

en: I will buy wine and beer.

u5-l1.15.en.en: We have cheese, but we don't have butter.
u5-l1.15.en.t: Bizda pishloq bor, lekin sariyogʻ yoʻq.

u5-l1.15.why.en: To say not, put **ne-** on the verb as one word: máme → **nemáme**. Nie sme is the not form of byť (we aren't), and nemajú is for oni.
u5-l1.15.why.t: Inkor uchun feʼlga **ne-** qoʻshib yoziladi: máme → **nemáme**. Nie sme — byť feʼlining inkori («biz … emasmiz»), nemajú esa oni uchun.

u5-l1.17.en.en: What do we need for the party?

en: After verbs like mať, potrebovať, kúpiť and hľadať (to look for), the object goes into the accusative case (akuzatív).
Feminine nouns change -a to **-u**. Masculine things and neuter nouns stay the same.
t: mať, potrebovať, kúpiť va hľadať (qidirmoq) kabi feʼllardan keyin toʻldiruvchi akuzatívda (tushum kelishigida) keladi. U oʻzbekcha «kimni? nimani?» savoliga javob beradi.
Ayol jinsidagi otlarda -a oʻrniga **-u** keladi. Erkak jinsidagi narsalar va oʻrta jins otlari oʻzgarmaydi.

u5-l2.1.why.en: Coffee is what you need, the object, so it takes the accusative: feminine nouns change -a to **-u**, káva → **kávu**.
u5-l2.1.why.t: Qahva — sizga kerak narsa, yaʼni toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun akuzatívda (tushum kelishigida) keladi: ayol jinsidagi otlarda -a oʻrniga **-u**, káva → **kávu**.

en: An adjective agrees with its noun. In the accusative, feminine -á becomes **-ú**.
With masculine things and neuter nouns, nothing changes.
t: Sifat oʻz otiga moslashadi. Akuzatívda (tushum kelishigida) ayol jinsidagi -á oʻrniga **-ú** keladi.
Erkak jinsidagi narsalar va oʻrta jins otlari bilan hech narsa oʻzgarmaydi.

u5-l2.3.why.en: An adjective agrees with its noun. Šunku is a feminine object, so čerstvá changes -á to **-ú**: **čerstvú**. Čerstvý is the masculine form.
u5-l2.3.why.t: Sifat oʻz otiga moslashadi. Šunku — ayol jinsidagi toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun čerstvá soʻzida -á oʻrniga **-ú** keladi: **čerstvú**. Čerstvý — erkak jinsi shakli.

u5-l2.5.why.en: After potrebovať, the object goes into the accusative: feminine nouns change -a to **-u**, so minerálka → **minerálku**.
u5-l2.5.why.t: potrebovať (kerak boʻlmoq) feʼlidan keyin toʻldiruvchi akuzatívda keladi: ayol jinsidagi otlarda -a oʻrniga **-u**, minerálka → **minerálku**.

u5-l2.6.why.en: Víno is neuter, and neuter nouns don't change as objects, so the adjective stays **dobré**. Dobrú is for feminine nouns, dobrého for male people.
u5-l2.6.why.t: Víno oʻrta jinsda, oʻrta jins otlari esa toʻldiruvchi boʻlganda oʻzgarmaydi, shuning uchun sifat ham **dobré** boʻlib qoladi. Dobrú ayol jinsi, dobrého esa erkak kishilar uchun.

u5-l2.7.en.en: I'll buy coffee and fresh bread.
u5-l2.7.en.t: Qahva va yangi non sotib olaman.

en: Ask **Koho?** (whom?) about people and **Čo?** (what?) about things.
Masculine nouns for people (and animals) add **-a**, and their adjectives end in **-ého**. Women follow the -u rule: Luci**a** → Luci**u**.
t: Odamlar haqida **Koho?** (kimni?), narsalar haqida **Čo?** (nimani?) deb soʻraladi.
Odamni (va hayvonni) bildiruvchi erkak jinsidagi otlarga **-a** qoʻshiladi, ularning sifatlari esa **-ého** bilan tugaydi. Ayollar -u qoidasiga boʻysunadi: Luci**a** → Luci**u**.

u5-l2.9.why.en: A brother is a person and the object of má, so the masculine noun adds **-a**: brat → **brata**. Only masculine things stay the same.
u5-l2.9.why.t: Aka — odam va má feʼlining toʻldiruvchisi, shuning uchun erkak jinsidagi ot **-a** oladi: brat → **brata**. Faqat erkak jinsidagi narsalar oʻzgarmaydi.

u5-l2.10.why.en: **Koho?** (whom?) asks about a person, so the answer names one: Marek → **Mareka**. Syr and kávu are things, which answer **Čo?**
u5-l2.10.why.t: **Koho?** (kimni?) odam haqida soʻraydi, shuning uchun javobda odam boʻladi: Marek → **Mareka**. Syr va kávu — narsalar, ular **Čo?** (nimani?) savoliga javob beradi.

u5-l2.11.prompt.en: We're looking for Tomáš and Lucia.

u5-l2.12.why.en: Kamarát is a male person, and as an object his adjective ends in **-ého**: **nového**. Nový is for masculine things, novú for feminine nouns.
u5-l2.12.why.t: Kamarát — erkak kishi, toʻldiruvchi boʻlganda uning sifati **-ého** bilan tugaydi: **nového**. Nový erkak jinsidagi narsalar, novú esa ayol jinsidagi otlar uchun.

u5-l3.0.note.en: Colours are adjectives, like nový: červen**é** víno = red wine.
u5-l3.0.note.t: Ranglar sifatdir, xuddi nový kabi: červen**é** víno = qizil vino.

u5-l3.1.note.en: biely and čierny have short endings: biel**a**, čiern**a**, and biel**u**, čiern**u** as objects (not -á, -ú). biele víno = white wine.
u5-l3.1.note.t: biely va čierny qisqa qoʻshimchalar oladi: biel**a**, čiern**a**, akuzatívda (tushum kelishigida) esa biel**u**, čiern**u** (-á, -ú emas). biele víno = oq vino.

u5-l3.5.why.en: An adjective takes the gender of its noun, after je too. Sukňa is feminine, so the colour ends in **-á**: červen**á**. Červený is masculine, červené neuter.
u5-l3.5.why.t: Sifat je soʻzidan keyin ham otning jinsiga moslashadi. Sukňa ayol jinsida, shuning uchun rang **-á** bilan tugaydi: červen**á**. Červený — erkak jinsi, červené — oʻrta jins.

u5-l3.6.note.en: chcieť = to want: chcem, chceš, chce… The colour takes the accusative too: čiern**u** sukň**u**.
u5-l3.6.note.t: chcieť = xohlamoq: chcem, chceš, chce… Rang ham akuzatívda (tushum kelishigida) keladi: čiern**u** sukň**u**.

u5-l3.7.en.en: I'm looking for a black skirt.

u5-l3.7.why.en: Sukňu is a feminine object, so the colour changes too. Čierny has short endings: čierna → **čiernu**, with -u, not -ú.
u5-l3.7.why.t: Sukňu — ayol jinsidagi toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun rang ham oʻzgaradi. Čierny qisqa qoʻshimchalar oladi: čierna → **čiernu**, -ú emas, -u bilan.

u5-l3.9.note.en: Emma and Tomáš are looking for a present for Lucia's party.
u5-l3.9.note.t: Emma va Tomash Lusiyaning bazmi uchun sovgʻa qidiryapti.

u5-l3.10.en.en: Emma and Tomáš are looking for a present.

u5-l3.11.en.en: What colour do you like? (to a woman)

u5-l3.11.note.en: mať rád (said of a man) / mať rada (of a woman) = to like. Mám rada zelen**ú** farb**u**. = I like green.
u5-l3.11.note.t: mať rád (erkak haqida) / mať rada (ayol haqida) = yoqtirmoq. Mám rada zelen**ú** farb**u**. = Men yashil rangni yoqtiraman.

u5-l3.13.why.en: Sveter is a masculine thing, and masculine things don't change as objects, so the colour stays **modrý**. Modrú is for feminine nouns, modrého for male people.
u5-l3.13.why.t: Sveter — erkak jinsidagi narsa, bunday otlar toʻldiruvchi boʻlganda oʻzgarmaydi, shuning uchun rang ham **modrý** boʻlib qoladi. Modrú ayol jinsi, modrého esa erkak kishilar uchun.

u5-l3.14.prompt.en: Emma is looking for a green T-shirt.

u5-l3.15.en.en: How much is the black sweater?

en: Pronouns have object forms too. The short forms go in second place in the sentence, like sa: Mám **ho** rád.
**ho** means both him and it: Sveter? Kúpim **ho**. = The sweater? I'll buy it.
t: Olmoshlarning ham akuzatív (tushum kelishigi) shakllari bor, oʻzbekcha meni, seni, uni kabi. Qisqa shakllar gapda ikkinchi oʻrinda turadi, xuddi sa kabi: Mám **ho** rád.
**ho** — erkak jinsidagi «uni»: odam haqida ham, narsa haqida ham: Sveter? Kúpim **ho**. = Sviter? Uni sotib olaman.

en: Where are you? I'm looking for you.

u5-l4.1.en.en: Where are you, Emma? I'm looking for you.

u5-l4.1.why.en: Emma is ty here, and as an object ty becomes **ťa**: hľadám ťa = I'm looking for you. Ju means her.
u5-l4.1.why.t: Bu yerda Emma — ty (sen), toʻldiruvchi boʻlganda esa ty **ťa** ga aylanadi, xuddi sen → seni kabi: hľadám ťa = seni qidiryapman. Ju — «uni» (ayolni).

en: **pre** (for) takes the accusative: darček pre Luci**u**, pre Tomáš**a**.
After a preposition, pronouns use their long forms.
t: **pre** (uchun) otdan oldin turadi va akuzatív (tushum kelishigi) talab qiladi: darček pre Luci**u** (Lusiya uchun sovgʻa), pre Tomáš**a**. Otdan oldin turadigan bunday soʻzlar predlog deyiladi.
Predlogdan keyin olmoshlarning uzun shakli ishlatiladi.

u5-l4.3.why.en: Tomáš is on, and the object form of on is **ho**, in second place: Mám **ho** rada. Ju is her, ich is them.
u5-l4.3.why.t: Tomash — on, on soʻzining toʻldiruvchi shakli esa **ho** (uni), u ikkinchi oʻrinda turadi: Mám **ho** rada. Ju — «uni» (ayolni), ich — «ularni».

u5-l4.4.why.en: After a preposition like **pre**, pronouns use their long forms: pre **teba**. Ťa is the short form, used without a preposition: hľadám ťa.
u5-l4.4.why.t: **pre** kabi predlogdan keyin olmoshlarning uzun shakli keladi: pre **teba** (sen uchun). Ťa — qisqa shakl, predlogsiz ishlatiladi: hľadám ťa.

u5-l4.5.why.en: **Pre** (for) takes the accusative, and Lucia follows the feminine -u rule: Lucia → **Luciu**.
u5-l4.5.why.t: **Pre** (uchun) akuzatív talab qiladi, Lucia esa ayol jinsidagi -u qoidasiga boʻysunadi: Lucia → **Luciu**.

en: Some verbs come with **na** + accusative: čakať na (to wait for), pozývať na (to invite to).
Pronouns use the long forms here too: na **teba**, na **neho**, na **ňu**.
t: Baʼzi feʼllar **na** + akuzatív (tushum kelishigi) bilan keladi: čakať na (…ni kutmoq), pozývať na (…ga taklif qilmoq).
Bu yerda ham olmoshlarning uzun shakli ishlatiladi: na **teba**, na **neho**, na **ňu**.

en: I'm inviting you to the party.

u5-l4.9.why.en: **Čakať na** takes the accusative, and masculine nouns for people add **-a**: Tomáš → **Tomáša**.
u5-l4.9.why.t: **Čakať na** (…ni kutmoq) akuzatív talab qiladi, odamni bildiruvchi erkak jinsidagi otlar esa **-a** oladi: Tomáš → **Tomáša** (Tomashni).

u5-l4.10.why.en: After a preposition like **na**, pronouns use their long forms: na **teba**. Ťa is the short form, used without a preposition, and ty isn't an object form.
u5-l4.10.why.t: **na** kabi predlogdan keyin olmoshlarning uzun shakli keladi: na **teba**. Ťa — predlogsiz ishlatiladigan qisqa shakl, ty esa toʻldiruvchi shakli emas.

u5-l4.11.prompt.en: We're inviting you to the party.

u5-l4.12.en.en: I'm inviting you to the party.

en: ísť (to go) is irregular, so learn it by heart.

Three prepositions often follow it, and they take the accusative. **na** = to (an event): Idem na oslav**u**. **po** = to go and get: Idem po chlieb. **cez** = through: Idem cez park (through the park).
t: ísť (bormoq) qoidaga boʻysunmaydi, shuning uchun uni yod oling.

Undan keyin koʻpincha uchta predlog keladi, ular akuzatív (tushum kelishigi) talab qiladi. **na** = …ga (tadbirga): Idem na oslav**u**. **po** = …ni olib kelishga: Idem po chlieb (nonga boryapman). **cez** = orqali: Idem cez park (park orqali).

en: Tomáš is going to get the wine.

u5-l5.1.why.en: The question is to Emma, **ty**, so ísť ends in **-eš**: ideš. Idem goes with ja, ide with on or ona.
u5-l5.1.why.t: Savol Emmaga berilyapti (ty), shuning uchun ísť **-eš** bilan tugaydi: ideš (boryapsan). Idem ja bilan, ide esa on yoki ona bilan keladi.

u5-l5.2.title.t: Xohlamoq, qila olmoq, majbur boʻlmoq + infinitív

en: chcieť (to want), môcť (can) and musieť (must, have to) are followed by an infinitive, the -ť form: ísť, kúpiť, piť (to drink).
Say no with ne-: nechcem, nemôžem, nemusím (I don't have to).
t: chcieť (xohlamoq), môcť (qila olmoq) va musieť (majbur boʻlmoq, kerak) feʼllaridan keyin infinitív keladi, yaʼni -ť bilan tugaydigan shakl (oʻzbekcha -moq kabi): ísť, kúpiť, piť (ichmoq).
Inkor ne- bilan yasaladi: nechcem, nemôžem, nemusím (shart emas).

en: What do you want to drink?

u5-l5.3.en.en: Lucia and Marek are going to the party.

u5-l5.3.why.en: Lucia and Marek are two people, **oni**, so ísť takes the oni form: **idú**. Ide is for one person, idete for vy.
u5-l5.3.why.t: Lusiya va Marek — ikki kishi, **oni**, shuning uchun ísť oni shaklida keladi: **idú**. Ide bitta kishi, idete esa vy uchun.

u5-l5.4.why.en: The speaker is **ja**, so musieť takes the ja form **musím**, followed by the infinitive ísť. Musia is for oni; môže means he or she can.
u5-l5.4.why.t: Gapiruvchi — **ja**, shuning uchun musieť ja shaklida: **musím**, undan keyin esa infinitív ísť keladi. Musia oni uchun, môže esa «u qila oladi» degani.

u5-l5.7.en.en: I'm going to get bread and wine.
u5-l5.7.en.t: Non va vino olib kelishga boryapman.

u5-l5.8.prompt.en: What do you want to drink?

en: **smieť** = to be allowed to. Careful: nesmieš = you mustn't, but nemusíš = you don't have to.
**vedieť** + infinitive = to know how to: Viem variť. = I can cook.
t: **smieť** = ruxsat boʻlmoq, mumkin boʻlmoq. Ehtiyot boʻling: nesmieš = mumkin emas (taqiqlangan), nemusíš esa = shart emas.
**vedieť** + infinitív = biror ishni qilishni bilmoq: Viem variť. = Men ovqat pishirishni bilaman.

u5-l5.10.why.en: **Vedieť** + infinitive means to know how to do something: viem variť = I can cook. I want to would be chcem, I have to musím.
u5-l5.10.why.t: **Vedieť** + infinitív — biror ishni qilishni bilmoq: viem variť = ovqat pishirishni bilaman. «Xohlayman» chcem, «majburman» esa musím boʻlardi.

en: You do not have to go.

u5-l5.13.why.en: Going through a place is **cez** + accusative: ideme cez park. **Na** is for going to an event, like na oslavu.
u5-l5.13.why.t: Biror joy orqali oʻtish — **cez** + akuzatív: ideme cez park. **Na** esa tadbirga borish uchun, masalan na oslavu.

u5-l6.1.en.t: Tugʻilgan kuning bilan! / Eng ezgu tilaklar!

u5-l6.1.note.en: The standard wish for birthdays and name days.
u5-l6.1.note.t: Tugʻilgan kun va ism kuni uchun odatiy tabrik (Slovakiyada har bir ismning kalendarda oʻz kuni bor).

u5-l6.2.question.en: It's your friend's birthday. What do you say?

u5-l6.3.note.en: One candle is sviečka. Plural things don't change as objects: Kúpime sviečky.
u5-l6.3.note.t: Bitta sham — sviečka. Koʻplikdagi narsalar akuzatívda (tushum kelishigida) oʻzgarmaydi: Kúpime sviečky.

u5-l6.4.note.en: Kúpime kytic**u**. = We'll buy a bouquet.

u5-l6.6.en.en: We'll buy a cake and candles.

u5-l6.6.why.en: The cake is what we'll buy, the object, so torta changes -a to **-u**: **tortu**. Sviečky is plural, and plural things don't change as objects.
u5-l6.6.why.t: Tort — sotib olinadigan narsa, toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun torta soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u** keladi: **tortu**. Sviečky — koʻplik, koʻplikdagi narsalar esa toʻldiruvchi boʻlganda oʻzgarmaydi.

u5-l6.7.en.en: Lots of health, happiness and love!

u5-l6.7.note.en: A classic birthday wish, often added after “Všetko najlepšie!”.
u5-l6.7.note.t: Tugʻilgan kunda aytiladigan anʼanaviy tilak, koʻpincha «Všetko najlepšie!» dan keyin qoʻshiladi.

u5-l6.10.note.en: ďakovať za + accusative: Ďakujem za kytic**u**.
u5-l6.10.note.t: ďakovať za + akuzatív (tushum kelishigi) = …uchun rahmat aytmoq: Ďakujem za kytic**u**.

u5-l6.11.why.en: **Ďakovať za** takes the accusative, so kytica changes -a to **-u**: za **kyticu**.
u5-l6.11.why.t: **Ďakovať za** (… uchun rahmat aytmoq) akuzatív talab qiladi, shuning uchun kytica soʻzida -a oʻrniga **-u** keladi: za **kyticu**.

u5-l6.12.en.en: When are you coming? — In an hour.

u5-l6.12.note.en: prísť (to come) works like ísť: prídem, prídeš, príde… o + accusative: o hodin**u** = in an hour.
u5-l6.12.note.t: prísť (kelmoq) ísť kabi tuslanadi: prídem, prídeš, príde… o + akuzatív (tushum kelishigi): o hodin**u** = bir soatdan keyin.

u5-l6.13.en.en: Tomáš is coming in an hour.

u5-l6.13.why.en: Tomáš is **on**, so prísť takes the on form, **príde**, just like ide. Prídem goes with ja, prídu with oni.
u5-l6.13.why.t: Tomash — **on**, shuning uchun prísť on shaklida keladi: **príde**, xuddi ide kabi. Prídem ja bilan, prídu esa oni bilan keladi.

en: I can't come, I have to work.
I cannot come, I have to work.
I can't come, I must work.

u5-l6.15.question.en: Marek raises his glass. What does he mean?
u5-l6.15.question.t: Marek qadahini koʻtaradi. U nima demoqchi?

u5-l6.16.prompt.en: I'll buy a bouquet for Lucia.

u5-l7.1.why.en: Sukňu is a feminine object of potrebuje, so its adjective changes -á to **-ú**: nová → **novú**. Nový is the masculine form.
u5-l7.1.why.t: Sukňu — potrebuje feʼlining ayol jinsidagi toʻldiruvchisi, shuning uchun sifatda -á oʻrniga **-ú** keladi: nová → **novú**. Nový — erkak jinsi shakli.

u5-l7.2.en.en: I'll buy fresh ham and cheese.
u5-l7.2.en.t: Yangi vetchina va pishloq sotib olaman.

u5-l7.3.en.en: Emma is looking for a white shirt.

u5-l7.3.why.en: Košeľu is a feminine object, so the colour changes too. Biely has short endings: biela → **bielu**, with -u, not -ú.
u5-l7.3.why.t: Košeľu — ayol jinsidagi toʻldiruvchi, shuning uchun rang ham oʻzgaradi. Biely qisqa qoʻshimchalar oladi: biela → **bielu**, -ú emas, -u bilan.

u5-l7.5.why.en: Kamarát is a male person, so as an object both words change: the noun adds **-a** and its adjective ends in **-ého**: nov**ého** kamarát**a**.
u5-l7.5.why.t: Kamarát — erkak kishi, shuning uchun toʻldiruvchi boʻlganda ikkala soʻz ham oʻzgaradi: ot **-a**, sifat esa **-ého** oladi: nov**ého** kamarát**a**.

u5-l7.6.why.en: After a preposition like **na**, on uses its long form: na **neho**. Ho is the short form, used without a preposition; ňu means her.
u5-l7.6.why.t: **na** kabi predlogdan keyin on uzun shaklda keladi: na **neho**. Ho — predlogsiz ishlatiladigan qisqa shakl, ňu esa «uni» (ayolni).

u5-l7.8.why.en: With **oni** (they), ísť ends in **-ú**: idú. Ide goes with on or ona, idem with ja.
u5-l7.8.why.t: **oni** (ular) bilan ísť **-ú** bilan tugaydi: idú. Ide on yoki ona bilan, idem esa ja bilan keladi.

en: Are you going to the party?

u5-l7.9.why.en: **Ideš** is the ty form of ísť (to go), and **na** + accusative means going to an event: na oslavu = to the party.
u5-l7.9.why.t: **Ideš** — ísť (bormoq) feʼlining ty shakli, **na** + akuzatív esa tadbirga borishni bildiradi: na oslavu = bazmga.

u5-l7.11.en.en: You're not allowed to smoke here.

u5-l7.11.why.en: Not allowed is **nesmieť**: nesmiete = you mustn't. Careful: nemusíte means you don't have to, and neviete you don't know how.
u5-l7.11.why.t: «Mumkin emas» — **nesmieť**: nesmiete = mumkin emas (taqiqlangan). Ehtiyot boʻling: nemusíte «shart emas», neviete esa «qila olmaysiz (bilmaysiz)» degani.

u5-l7.14.en.en: I'm inviting you to the party.
